summary: Robert Gauthiot was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études. In 1909, he became a member of the Société Asiatique.
Robert Göbl worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as history and archaeology. After studying at the University of Vienna from 1947 to 1950, he held a post there from circa 1955 to 1989.

A Japanologist, Robert H. Brower studied at Harvard and the University of Michigan. He taught at the University of Minnesota and Stanford before serving at Michigan from 1966 to 1988, including as department chair, and directing the Inter-University Center (1963–1964).

Robert H. Sharf specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, having studied at Toronto, Kyoto, and Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez. His career includes posts at McMaster, Michigan (1995–2003), and UC Berkeley, where he became a distinguished professor circa 2004.
Robert Hinde studied at St John's College (~1941–1947) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1947–1950). He subsequently held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1950 to 1989.

Robert J. Miller was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served on the faculty and as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from circa 1955 to 1989, and was also a professor at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

Robert J. Topmiller is a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Kentucky, where he studied under doctoral supervisor George C. Herring.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Robert Kritzer completed his doctorate at the University of California, Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini by 1995. He held posts at Berkeley and served as Associate Professor at Kyoto Notre Dame University (attested 1999–2017).
Robert Kyd studied at the University of Edinburgh. In 1787, he founded the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden.

Robert L. Brown worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a curator of South and Southeast Asian art at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (~1980–2014) and Professor Emeritus of Art History at UCLA (~1986–2014).

Robert Lenz studied at the University of Tartu and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp. He held posts at Tallinn Cathedral School, the University of Breslau, and the Austrian Academy of Sciences, serving as Professor of Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University (~1835–1836).

Robert M. Gimello worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology, earning his PhD from Columbia University (~1969–1976). He served at the University of Arizona (~1981–2020), including as department head and professor emeritus, and as professor at Harvard University (~2001–2006).

Robert Maclagan was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Edinburgh, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and the Royal School of Military Engineering. From 1847 to 1860, he served as Principal of the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee.

Robert Magliola works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD from Princeton (~1966–1970). He held posts at Purdue, Tamkang, Assumption University of Thailand, National Taiwan University, and Columbia University.

A specialist in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Robert Mayer studied at the University of Bristol and completed his PhD at Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter, Alexis Sanderson, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen. In 2002, he was an Oriental Studies faculty member at Oxford.

A scholar in linguistics and Indology, Robert Needham Cust studied at Eton, Trinity College Cambridge, East India Company College, and Fort William College. He served in the Bengal Civil Service from circa 1843 to 1867.

Indologist Robert P. Goldman studied at Columbia and the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher, also studying under T. S. Srinivasa Sastri and Shivram Dattatray Joshi. He held appointments at the University of California, Berkeley from circa 1971, becoming Professor Emeritus circa 2020.

Robert P. Scharlemann specialized in religious studies and philosophy, studying at Concordia College, Concordia Seminary, and Heidelberg University. He held academic posts at the University of Southern California (~1963–1966), the University of Iowa (~1966–1981), and the University of Virginia (~1981–2003).

A scholar of religious studies and Japanology, Robert S. Ellwood studied at the University of Colorado, Yale University, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. He subsequently held a faculty post at the University of Southern California from circa 1967 to 1997.

Robert S. Nelson is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Rice University (~1965–1969) and New York University (~1970–1978). He held professorial appointments at the University of Chicago (~1974–2005) and Yale University (~2005–2021).
